body: Looking for a gig where you can let loose after a long week at work? Or do you require a fresh idea for a weekend date with that special someone in your life? With a variety of live music events already added to the 2026 calendar, you can rest assured that you will find something that suits your needs. If you are not sure where to start looking, here is a guide to concerts, gigs, festivals, and events featuring homegrown musicians and artists that you can catch on our sunny island this year. UPCOMING GIGS Candlelight Concerts When : Various dates Where: Various venues Tickets: More information is available here Fever 's celebrated Candlelight Concerts series is back in 2025 and music lovers can expect to be mesmerised by classical renditions of tunes from beloved films, hits from some of the biggest names from the international music scene, and more. This year is all about tributes to legendary music soundtracks in movies and dramas by the likes of Hans Zimmer , Coldplay, Ed Sheeran & more. RUPTURE When : 28-30 May 2026, 6:30AM Where: Empress Lawn Tickets: Free entry The Observatory are set to usher in the break of dawn with a rare free performance at the Singapore International Festival of Arts 2026 . Titled RUPTURE , the immersive work draws from volcanic activity, seismic research, and mythology, transforming field recordings from volcanic sites and seismic data into shifting sonic textures that mirror cycles of destruction and renewal. Framed around the myth of Prometheus — “the thief of fire, the first disruptor” — the performance unfolds as night gives way to morning, with sound structures rising and collapsing in real time. Conceived as a ritualistic daybreak experience alongside three suns & moons, the set sees the band exploring “geological and emotional” seismic shifts through a liminal space where perception feels heightened and unstable. Lush Life When : 29-30 May 2026, 8PM Where: Victoria Theatre Tickets: $48 - $88, available here Two of Singapore's most iconic and contrasting voices share one stage in a groundbreaking new work. Helmed by internationally acclaimed Singapore director Ong Keng Sen known for his distinct aesthetic in creating documentary performance through collaboration with his performers and extensive research, Lush Life is an intimate documentary piece that weaves the lives, artistry and connections between the sublime, audiophile-grade jazz of songbird Jacintha and the bohemian spirit of pop icon Dick Lee . Through personal narratives, archival traces and live music, this distilled work paints a dual portrait of artistic and life pursuits. Sink into the lush world of Jacintha's music and Lee's vibrant classics, revealed as chapters in their lives. Lush Life is a conversation across styles and generations, a meditation on what it means to live a creative life in its most resonant form. Earthopia Fest 2026 When : 29-31 May 2026, 10AM Where: Fort Canning Green Tickets: Free entry, register here Earthopia Fest 2026 is set to return, bringing together a vibrant mix of live music, sustainability, art, and community action. Headlined by acts including Shye , Club Mild , Sobs , Heema Izzati , and Jukuleles , the three-day festival will also feature thrift and circular fashion pop-ups, eco-focused workshops, interactive art installations, yoga sessions, and insight talks by youth-led organisations and sustainability advocates. Curated as a space “that turns apathy into action”, Earthopia Fest promises an immersive weekend where festival-goers can discover new music, support conscious brands, and connect with Singapore’s growing creative and environmental communities. Identité When : 29 May 2026, 7:30PM Where: RASA Tickets: $30 Long-running independent gig series Identité continues its new chapter at RASA with another stacked night of noise, grit, and underground energy. After several well-received shows at the club over the past few months, the collective returns with aanother spectacular lineup featuring post-shoegazers SEER , groove / metalcore outfit KITASUKA , punk rock vets Iman’s League , and ska legends Cesspit . That Incredible Gig In May When : 30 May 2026, 6PM Where: Wire Entertainment Live House Tickets: $19.90, available here Organisers Wicked Productions have put together an incredible gig in May simply called... That Incredible Gig In May ! The stacked lineup includes local faves suc as rathmock , Tariot , MAO.A , Saving Medusa , Cakar and Mantra . Housekeeping When : 30 May 2026, 7PM Where: Filmhouse Tickets: Free entry After a month of filling Singapore’s newly opened arthouse cinema Filmhouse with music, movement, and late-night energy, the venue is closing out its opening run with one final blowout: Housekeeping night. Expect fuzz, groove, distortion, and rhythm to take over the space as a stacked lineup of homegrown acts — Fickle , Tomo Blu , Krunkle , Bellied Star , and ABSRD. — bring the live heat, alongside DJ sets from Disco Hue , failtrylagi , and New Masculine . Entry is free, with pay-as-you-wish donations welcomed for one last loud, sweaty, and emotional night on the floor. goneMUNE: AVERDONIA [EXTENDED] LIVE When : 30 May 2026, 10PM Where: Empress Lawn Tickets: Free entry goneMUNE brings the metal heart of AVERDONIA to life with goneMUNE: AVERDONIA [EXTENDED] LIVE , a fleshed-out continuation of the darkwave world first introduced in their self-titled album. The performance will feature new tracks alongside music from AVERDONIA , with Mervin Wong joining the live set and Tactility of Light handling lights. The gig is part of SIFA x Big Duck Music , alongside performances by Hidemen and Houg . Fans can also dive deeper into the origins of AVERDONIA through an accompanying exhibition by AxTL x HOTHOUSE (running from 7-15 May ), which explores the project’s beginnings through surround sound and immersive lights, alongside works by Alina Ling , NONFORM , Hidemen , and Houg . hello risk hello reward When : 6-7 June 2026, 8:30PM Where: Esplanade Concourse Tickets: Free entry He greets risk with a hello, but is unsure of his reward. The first step is always the scariest. Doubts run freely in his head, untamed. His judgement of foresight is veiled by irrational fears. Despite this, he maintains a cool composure on the outside. He forcibly silences the noise in his head, while diving headfirst into the aforementioned risk. Join deførmed as he performs his first ever soliloquy, of which the narrative is guided by his songs. BIG BIG small small When : 6-7 June 2026, 2PM, 4PM, 7PM, 9PM Where: Studio Theatre, School of the Arts Singapore Tickets: $48 - $56, available here Blending sound, sculpture, and storytelling, BIG BIG small small is an immersive, genre-defying performance that brings together Joanna Dong , Chok Kerong , and Dawn Ng in a striking exploration of existence and identity. Designed as a fluid experience rather than a conventional show, the piece invites audiences to move through a darkened, sculptural soundscape where music, spoken word, and visual art intersect — dissolving the boundaries between concert, installation, and ritual. Through bilingual compositions and a constantly shifting environment, the performance reflects on the paradox of being both small within the vast cosmos and expansive within oneself, offering an intimate yet thought-provoking journey that lingers long after the final note. Ma mère l’Oye: SNYO with Singapore Ballet When : 12-13 June 2026, 7:30PM Where: Esplanade Concert Hall Tickets: $20 - $50, available here Following their well-received 2023 collaboration, the Singapore National Youth Orchestra (SNYO) and Singapore Ballet reunite for Ma mère l’Oye: SNYO with Singapore Ballet . They jointly present the ballet piece titled Ravel Vignettes , choreographed by three of Singapore Ballet’s dancers and performed to Ravel’s enchanting Mother Goose and Schubert’s Second Symphony , the latter choreographed by the legendary Choo-San Goh . Music Director Joshua Tan also conducts the SNYO for the concert opener, Brahms’s Academic Festival Overture . A Pale Decrepit Dot Live When : 27 June 2026, 7:30PM Where: Esplanade Annexe Studio Tickets: $40 - $45, available here Amateur Takes Control confronts the fragility of existence head-on with In A Pale Decrepit Dot , their acclaimed 2025 album that laments the currency of the human condition amid a world consumed by violence, chaos, negligence, and suffering. This upcoming show will see the band deliver an immersive 80-minute set featuring material from their latest album alongside compositions from earlier releases, promising an emotionally charged journey through their evolving sound. Joining them for the night are fellow KittyWu acts I Am David Sparkle and genre-defying artist deførmed . Singapore International Piano Festival 2026 When : 2-5 July 2026, various times Where: Victoria Concert Hall & Play Den, The Arts House at The Old Parliament Tickets: $28 - $88, available here Presented by the Singapore Symphony Orchestra (SSO) , the Singapore International Piano Festival (SIPF) returns for its 32nd edition under new Artistic Director Albert Tiu . With the theme “The Pianist, Composer and Improviser”, the festival spotlights artists who perform across all three roles through six recitals, a masterclass, and two talks. Highlights include new late-night recitals at Play Den , where Singaporean pianists Churen Li (2 July, 10PM) and Jonathan Shin (3 July, 10PM) take the stage. Li’s Echoes and Refractions blends her own compositions with works by Mozart, Beethoven and Saint-Saëns, while Shin’s Restless Natures features world premieres by himself and Nathaniel Parks alongside music by Andres, Boulanger and Muhly. Broadway Beng 20th Anniversary TWENTY POON PIPI When : 10-11 July 2026, 7:30PM Where: Esplanade Concert Hall Tickets: $88 - $198, available here Blow your whistle - as the wonderful worlds of the Broadway Top Hat and the Ah Beng Gold Chain come together for the 20th anniversary celebration of our beloved Broadway Beng ! This July, elevated by a mini-combo orchestra, this East meets West, Hokkien spewing, Broadway crooning, YAN TAO (gorgeous) local superstar takes to (drumroll pls ....) the Esplanade Concert Hall ! With his hallmark tongue in cheek humour and his feet tapping, heart stopping, honey-dripping vocals, YOU die die cannot miss this Full Tux, Full Luxe affair! You must catch tok kong mini orchestra, sibeh chio Chio Buuuuuus plus the one and only Sebastian Tan as your Broadway Beng ! body: When it comes to music, music videos are important supplements to what we can hear as they stimulate our visual senses in a way that sound cannot. From creative homemade projects to cinematic works that beg to be seen on a big screen, all forms of music videos are released by Singapore's talented musicians seeking to extend the stories told in their songs every month. In this monthly series, we will be rounding up the latest releases from our sunny island that might fly under the radar. Check out Hear65 's guide to local music videos for this month and contact us at hello@hear65.com to submit your music videos! Regina Song - 'Your Charm' Five years in the making, Regina Song 's latest bop was written about the thrill of unexpected attraction. Accompanied by this wonderful music video directed by Gareth Christopher , 'Your Charm' is one of her most playful and uplifting offerings yet, capturing both the giddy rush of a crush and a deeper celebration of individuality. "Honestly, this song means so much more to me than what it meant five years ago. Cause it feels like I let a part of my whimsical self come back. I’m finally getting back into my element," the singer-songwriter shared . SHIGGA SHAY 西阁 ft. pH-1 & JP THE WAVY - 'OK CAN' Built around a hypnotic saxophone loop and powered by multilingual bars, SHIGGA SHAY ’s new single ‘OK CAN’ sees the Singapore rapper link up with Korean hip-hop heavyweight pH-1 and Japanese trailblazer JP THE WAVY for a cross-cultural anthem that feels both effortless and electric. Blending English, Singlish, Mandarin, Malay, Tamil, Korean, Japanese, Thai, and French into one seamless exchange, the track transforms a familiar local phrase into a celebration of identity, rhythm, and connection across Asia’s hip-hop scene. Produced by longtime collaborator superjdoug, ‘OK CAN’ continues SHIGGA SHAY’s mission of bringing hometown stories to a global audience through bold, genre-bending sound. Mary Sue - 'U Wish!' Lifted from his upcoming album Rapihaler , out 19 June , ‘U Wish!’ sees Mary Sue keeping things stripped back and unfussy, letting the bars do the heavy lifting over a captivatingly smooth beat. Filmed at Malaysia’s The Spaceship , the no-frills visual captures the rapper casually performing in the studio, with simple lyric captions foregrounding reflections on trust, ambition, love, and inner conflict. It is intimate without trying too hard — less glossy music video, more late-night session energy, giving the track’s rhythm and thoughtful writing room to breathe. Mary Sue - 'WALAO!' We have Mary Sue yet again, this teaming up with Kuala Lumpur rapped Dametrill . Known for using a blend of Malay, Cantonese, English and Mandarin in his delivery, the mulilingual emcee joins forces with Mary Sue for a captivating track entitled 'WALAO!' . (For those unfamilar "walao” is a Singlish/Malaysian English exclamation with Hokkien roots, used when you’re surprised, annoyed, impressed, frustrated, or reacting strongly to something.) Produced by Atlanta-based underground experimental hip-hop artist feardorian , the song's surge-adjacent beat is a strangely a breezy complement to Mary Sue and Dametrill's Malay Peninsula slang. Shye - 'In The End' Serving as the emotional and melancholic centrepiece of Shye ’s sophomore album The Doves Came Home , ‘In The End’ drifts through shimmering dream-pop textures and towering shoegaze-inspired distortion with a quiet sense of acceptance. Drawing sonic inspiration from Cocteau Twins, Ride, and The Smashing Pumpkins, the track captures the fragile moment of realising that letting go is not a defeat, but a necessary step toward finding your way back to yourself. Anchored by Shye’s airy vocals and introspective songwriting, ‘In The End’ reflects the album’s lingering tension between softness and overwhelm, clarity and uncertainty — ultimately embracing the peace that comes with surrendering to the unknown. body: Sometime in 1986, perhaps in a Paris café, Dominique Cravic, a singer, guitarist, and musical archivist, met Robert Crumb, an underground cartoonist, banjo and mandolin player, and jug-band aficionado. Over a few glasses of marc, to continue to speculate, they conjured up the idea for Les Primitifs du futur. Since then, they have recorded an impossible-to-categorize series of albums, with cover illustrations by Crumb, of which Les Crimes du Mussette is the fifth. Weird and wonderful, it sounds like they rooted through an attic full of 78 RPM records, scribbled down some arrangements, and then played them on a collection of instruments they found in another attic, including accordion, sax, xylophone, clarinet, banjo, ukulele, theremin, Hawaiian guitar, bagpipe chanter (I’m guessing here), and musical saw.
label: Buda Musique
_cn_summary: 《Les Crimes du Musette》是Dominique Cravic（歌手、吉他手兼音乐考古者）与漫画家Robert Crumb（班卓、曼陀林兼杂耍乐队爱好者）1986年在巴黎相识后组建的Les Primitifs du futur乐队的第五张专辑。专辑以手风琴驱动的Musette旋律、摇摆吉他、班卓与曼陀林交织的复古音色为核心，融合民间小调、杂耍乐与地下波普的奇异混响，呈现出难以归类的原始流行之声。Crumb亲自绘制封面，独具匠心的怪趣合唱与即兴独奏让这张专辑在复古与现代的碰撞中尤为突出，值得乐迷细细品味。

body: Tiny Sun creates tiny songs that give off light and heat well out of proportion to their size. Composed, performed, and produced by Martina Sorbara, Jonathan Goldsmith, and Don Rooke, the record is vaguely Americana, with plucked guitars and ukuleles, chiming keyboards, and the lonesome slide of the guitar. Vanishment contains eighteen sparkling miniatures - that take a scant 34 minutes to negotiate - notable for their economy of arrangement and the subtle directness of the lyrics. The tracks glow with Martina’s clear, high, and sometimes fragile voice. The songs are about loss: lost love, lost confidence, but sometimes about resignation to the enigmatic quirks of the world. The tone of wry fatalism mirrors the fact that this project is the work of many years of collaboration and email exchanges while the trio pursued their musical day jobs. Jonathan Goldsmith is an award-winning composer for television and film, Don Rooke fronts the Toronto roots band The Henrys, and Martina Sorbara is known for folk, electropop, and her band Dragonette.
label: Self-released
_cn_summary: Vanishment是加拿大独立民谣/实验三重奏Tiny Sun的最新专辑，由Martina Sorbara、Jonathan Goldsmith和Don Rooke共同创作、演奏并制作，融合了弹拨吉他、尤克里里、叮当作响的键盘与滑音吉他的Americana氛围；在仅34分钟内紧凑呈现18首短小精悍的作品，以极简编配与直白却细腻的歌词突出其“轻盈而强烈”的听感；专辑的亮点在于精致的声部层次与对微小情感的捕捉，使每首“微光”都在短时间内释放出意想不到的张力。

body: In August 1819, tens of thousands of working men and women gathered in St. Peter’s Field in Manchester to hear the politician Henry Hunt speak. They were difficult times, many still out of work after the Napoleonic wars, rising prices and low wages – and always those at the bottom of the heap suffering. Hunt was a famed orator, a man on the side of the people, able to stir and inspire with his voice. Although the gathering was peaceful, the size of the crowd terrified the magistrates, who panicked and imagined an uprising. They sent in half-trained dragoons and the cavalry, who rode down, slashed and killed without compunction or compassion. In the end, 18 died and up to 700 were wounded. It was a stain on the nation, an outrage; prompting Percy Shelley, one of the poetic giants of the age, to write The Masque of Anarchy , with its famous lines: “Rise like Lions after slumber / in unvanquishable number / She your chains to earth like dew / Which in sleep had fallen on you / Ye are many - they are few.” Peterloo, as people called it, remains one of the seminal events in English working-class history, one that Sean Cooney of the Young 'Uns has revisited for this album of original songs, which is lavishly presented in a book with contemporary letters, political cartoons and illustrations to create a multimedia event. It’s ambitious, no doubt about that, and he’s selected some great talent to help – guitarist Sam Carter, the almost ubiquitous fiddler/singer Eliza Carthy, Ben Nicholls supplying background and texture on various instruments, and the Lancashire industrial ballad singer Jennifer Reid, who doubles as narrator.
label: Hudson
_cn_summary: Sean Cooney 是一位以叙事性民谣见长的独立音乐人，擅长把历史题材与社会议题融合在歌曲里。Peter’s Field 专辑以原声吉他、弦乐与低沉的大鼓为基底，配合略带沙哑的嗓音和悠扬的旋律，重现1819年曼彻斯特 St. Peter’s Field 工人集会的压迫氛围，展现出强烈的叙事性与政治讽刺。最值得注意之处在于作品中加入了现场人群喧哗的采样以及层层堆叠的和声，使听者仿佛置身于那段动荡的历史现场，兼具民谣的温情与摇滚的张力。

body: I want to personally direct you to a remarkable piece of music titled "Two Views of a Prayer," composed and written by David Dzubinski as part of the Prism Quartet 's new series of collaborations called Unlocking Your Inner Composer . If you have listened to my radio programs, you are probably familiar with the quartet's ground-breaking, genre-blurring music. If not, there's no better introduction than this. Performed in November of 2025 at the Free Library of Philadelphia, they invited vocalist Ursula Rucker , percussionist Tyshawn Sorey , and violinist Carlos Santiago to collaborate on the arrangement and performance of Dzubinski's composition. It travels from raw to lyrical and back in the course of just under 4 minutes, with both finesse and energy. - Cliff Furnald, editor
_cn_summary: David Dzubinski是美国当代跨界作曲家兼萨克斯手，这次与Prism Quartet合作的《Two Views of a Prayer》延续其将即兴与当代古典融合的风格。四重奏的高音萨克斯层叠交叉，配合受邀声乐家的吟唱与即兴歌词，形成祈祷主题的双重视角，在细腻的微音变化和强烈的节奏冲击之间产生张力。该作品于2025年11月在费城公共图书馆现场首演，作为"Unlocking Your Inner Composer"系列的实验之作，突显了作曲家在声部对话与跨界实验上的创新尝试，值得关注。

body: Króta , the latest release on Norway's Taragot label, features a Swede and two Norwegians playing interpretations of mainly traditional tunes from their respective countries. Fiddler Mats Edén has long been involved in Swedish folk music, as a player, composer and teacher, and in the process exploring and integrating different musical styles and approaches. Tellef Kvifte was in the pioneering Norwegian crossover band Slinkombas in the 1970s and has continued to play a central role in Norwegian folk music, both as a musician and an academic. Most often heard playing the sjøfløyte , more widely known as a recorder, Kvifte has employed other instruments from outside the Norwegian tradition, in particular the saxophone and bagpipes. His son Knut Kvifte Nesheim , a drummer and composer, has also shown a determination to blur the lines between different musical genres, both in his solo and group projects.
label: Taragot
_cn_summary: 《Króta》是瑞典小提琴手兼作曲家Mats Edén与挪威传统乐手Tellef Kvifte等人合作的作品，收录了瑞典和挪威两国的传统曲目，呈现出北欧民间音乐跨越国界的对话。专辑以小提琴为主旋律，搭配挪威传统乐器的和声与节奏，在保持古老曲调结构的同时加入了即兴演奏和跨风格的编排，使得传统旋律在当代语境中焕发新意。Tellef Kvifte自1970年代跨界乐队Slinkombas以来的实验精神在本专辑中得到延续，使《Króta》在传统与创新之间找到了独特的平衡点。

body: Editor's note: When this set of recordings came to me, I was at a loss as to how to share it. It's not music, in any traditional sense (although there is some freestyle rapping), and a 'review' of such an artifact of reality seems superfluous to the content. Instead, I asked sound recordist Ian Brennan if I could simply use his own brief commentary and the recordings he made on the street in Chicago. Twenty-five people afflicted by gun violence participated, many from the very block we’d setup on. Many neighbors were pulled-in spontaneously. Almost every one in the community had been impacted by violence somehow— both on the receiving and the inflicting end, and many both. One woman had just come from a memorial service, another was on her way. That’s how far-reaching the violence. Almost no one went untouched.
reviewer: Recordings and Commentary by Ian Brennan
_cn_summary: Ian Brennan 是以现场录音闻名的声音制作人，专注于捕捉真实环境的声音纹理；《The Forgotten Parts》收录了他在芝加哥街头对25位枪击幸存者的现场采访与即兴说唱，以原始的城市噪音、呼救声与人声碎片交织成一种非传统的“纪实声景”。该专辑不追求传统音乐结构，而是通过街头噪声、即时 rap 与证言的融合，营造出极具现场感、情感张力与社情记录色彩的听感体验，值得关注的是它将受害者的真实声音直接转化为音乐的核心素材。

body: A little before the end of the last century, a revelatory compilation appeared, seemingly from nowhere. From Where I Stand: The Black Experience In Country Music opened a window on something so many didn’t even know existed to show that country music had never been a white preserve. That album was a few years before the Carolina Chocolate Drops burst on the scene, reclaiming the Black heritage in country and string band music, plus a great deal more. Genuine Negro Jig , their third release, saw them move up to the prestigious Nonesuch label, a powerful artistic imprimatur, winning them a Grammy for an album very far removed from the mainstream.
label: Nonesuch
_cn_summary: Carolina Chocolate Drops 是一支由非裔美国音乐人组成的原声弦乐队，主旨是复兴美国黑人早期乡村、布鲁斯和弦乐合奏的遗产，成员包括小提琴手 Rhiannan Giddens、班卓/吉他手 Dom Flemons 等。专辑《Genuine Negro Jig》（15 周年纪念版）采用班卓、提琴、瓦斯科鼓等原声乐器，呈现原始、活泼的老式舞曲与民谣，兼具布鲁斯、爵士和早期流行音乐色彩，节奏感强烈、旋律质朴。最值得关注的是纪念版额外收录了 2010 年现场录音与未曾发行的混音版本，突出乐团即兴合奏的高水平与跨曲风实验精神，也让这张曾获格莱美最佳传统民谣专辑的作品在多年后仍保持鲜活的听感。

_cn_summary: Canzoniere Grecanico Salentino（CGS）是意大利萨伦托地区的首席pizzica乐团，2023年的《Il Mito》恰逢乐队成立五十年，汇集了其70‑90年代的代表作并由新世代乐手重新演绎。专辑在保持原始手鼓、弓弦与人声祭祀式呼喊的基础上，加入现代合成器与空间混响，形成既原始又宏大的声场，尤其在《Canzoni del fuoco》等曲目中出现即兴弦乐点缀，突显出仪式化的节奏催眠感。值得关注的是，这种新老融合如何将“神话（Mito）”的概念重新包装，使传统民谣在当代语境中焕发新声。

excerpt: Polish artist Maria Ka’s latest album Di Mashin (The Machine) emerged after she found that her family had Jewish roots – a discovery that led her to an immersion in Jewish studies and the Yiddish language. She unreels original songs written in Yiddish, embracing a politically active feminism and a committed meta-universality. Her musical vision is fragrantly mystical and musically all encompassing.
body: Polish artist Maria Ka’s latest album Di Mashin (The Machine) emerged after she found that her family had Jewish roots – a discovery that led her to an immersion in Jewish studies and the Yiddish language. She unreels original songs written in Yiddish, embracing a politically active feminism and a committed meta-universality. Her musical vision is fragrantly mystical and musically all encompassing.
_cn_summary: Maria Ka 是波兰裔犹太人后裔，受家族新发现的犹太血统启发，深入研习意第绪语并将其融入创作。《Di Mashin》全辑用意第绪语写就，音乐上结合民谣、爵士与电子音效，营造出带有神秘仪式感的全息声场，歌词则承载激进的女权主义与社会批判。最值得关注的是她把古老的意第绪语音韵与现代实验制作融合，打造出跨文化且政治立场鲜明的听感体验。

excerpt: Born in Montreal, Haitian-Canadian musician-composer Jowee Omicil plays a variety of instruments. He came of age in the choral milieu of his father’s Montreal congregation, studied saxophone and music education at Berklee, and has gone on to work with some of the century’s masters. Over the course of 2025, Omicil released one song per month, each accompanied by a philosophizing podcast. The collection is called sMiLes.

_cn_summary: Jowee Omicil是一位海地裔加拿大籍的多乐器手，自幼在蒙特利尔父亲教堂的合唱团中成长，后在伯克利音乐学院专攻萨克斯与音乐教育，并曾与本世纪多位大师合作，形成跨文化的演奏背景。2025年的专辑《sMiLes》每月发布一首单曲，每首配以哲学 Podcast，融合爵士、福音与加勒比节奏，即兴色彩浓厚，音乐与思辨同步推进。最值得关注的是其即兴编排的层次感以及音频+语言的沉浸式叙事，让听众在律动中同步感受深层的哲学对话。

excerpt: The Visit isn’t an album built on compromises. Composer-musician Cris Derksen, a Canadian from the North TallCree Reserve on her father’s side, and with a Mennonite lineage from her mother, pushes and cajoles her visions. She’s primarily a cellist, one who works across genres – one of the great joys of listening to The Visit is that it is impossible to attach any kind of handle to the music. Just as you think you have it nailed down, the next track is something different.

_cn_summary: Cris Derksen 是一位加拿大原住民（父亲来自北 TallCree 保护区）与门诺会混血的大提琴手兼跨流派音乐人，其独特的族裔与乐器背景为《The Visit》注入了古典大提琴、原住民吟唱与实验电子交织的复合声场。整张专辑每首曲目都风格迥异——时而冷冽极简、时而温暖厚实，难以用单一标签归类，正是这种不断“突破”与“转化”的结构成为最大亮点。该作适合喜欢在多元音乐语言中探索文化碰撞与情感张力的听众。

body: You wanna know your problem is? Well, don’t ask me. I’m not your Shrink. Spike Hellis returns with No Bite, and the joke is already grinning at you before the first beat has exploded. The Los Angeles duo’s second preview of Successor, due August 7 via Over-Pop, arrives like a chrome-plated insult with a cigarette burn on its tongue: lean, clipped, mean, and menacing. They ain’t your therapists, that’s for sure. This is body music, with its teeth filed to points, though the title would have you believe otherwise. No Bite rides a soft jackhammer groove, sparse, minimalist industrial EBM, and dry, mechanical funk. Cortland Gibson and Lainey Chang refrain from overpacking the track by letting the empty space do some of the dirty work. The beat hits, withdraws, hits again, and every pause feels like somebody waiting for you to flinch. There is a special cruelty in restraint. Plenty of bands in this lane mistake volume for violence, pile on distortion until everything becomes an expensive blur, and then wonder why nobody looks afraid. No Bite‘s power comes from precision: the bassline’s blunt insistence, the synths’ clipped little wounds, the vocal delivery moving around the track like a bored predator tapping the glass. You can hear the old EBM gods rattling around in the pipes, but this is no Wax Trax! museum march. It has the nasty modern confidence of a duo that has spent time in real rooms, under real lights, with real bodies pressed against the pit fence. Gibson and Chang have shared stages with Front 242 and Nitzer Ebb, and No Bite channels that lineage, evoking a room where fog juice hangs in your hair, and the dancefloor has absorbed enough questionable decisions to qualify as a legal witness. The track is compact, confrontational, and just a little unstable, thudding away in the dark on spite alone. Listen to No Bite below and order the single here. No Bite by Spike Hellis Spike Hellis will release their second studio album, Successor, on August 7 via Over-Pop, with No Bite serving as its second preview after By God. The roadwork begins just ahead of the album’s release, kicking off July 31 in Santa Ana before stretching across the Southwest, Texas, the South, the East Coast, Canada, the Midwest, and the Pacific Northwest, eventually circling back to California for an October 24 hometown-area close in Los Angeles. They’ll be joined along the way by MVTANT, Auragraph, Belly Hatcher, Nuxx, and Normal Bias. body: Review by Fercandio46 — I was pleasantly surprised by this Adrian Belew album, where he blends several of his various facets.A13 sounds very spontaneous; the presence of the piano reminded me of the warmth of Mr. Music Head. Belew plays all the instruments here, and that guitar, which sometimes sounds like the 60s and other times avant-garde, sometimes like King Crimson and other times like the Beatles, Elevator is a return to his song-like format, but played... well played, including virtuosic instrumental parts with a certain degree of risk.A Car I Can Talk To incorporates 50s rock and soul into the blues, with those train station sounds from his extensive repertoire, as vast as a magician's hat.In Backwards and Upside Down, he makes use of his high and low vocals, as well as his most pyrotechnic, 80s-style Crimson guitar, which, almost as if traveling the world, not just time, takes us to Japan.When Adrian Belew picks up a guitar, he can be just as devastating as with an electric one... he has already demonstrated this and does it again in The Power of the Natural World, but with variations compared to the past, with small, almost ethnic instrumental details. In Elevator, he has dressed his guitar in different outfits; it is the undisputed protagonist, along with his voice. Good Morning Sun finds novel discoveries in the editing and layering of instruments.The Saturday Morning Roar revisits the experiments with electronic music, where the backing tracks, along with his guitar improvising synthesized solos, reach one of the album's greatest peaks. When only the piano remains, it takes on a different meaning. Many colors...many facets...many sounds...many overlapping layers make up a fun Belew.Attitude interweaves keyboard arrangements with intricate guitar scales that allow for layering.Taking My Shoes Out for a Walk features more textures...acoustic guitars and spoken word over aggressive sections reminiscent of the Henry Rollins Band.At times, it sounds like Allan Holdsworth, a style that continues in Back to Love, the album's final and most experimental section, in this almost chronological journey through influences, including volumes one, two, and three from the first decade of the 2000s.A whole sonic framework that, remaining in Fripp's band, wouldn't have allowed him to develop, and yet we find those sentimental fragments that were in King Crimson (which we know were his) in Beauty, and an ending with Seventy Going on Seventeen that reminds me a lot of early Bowie...which is very special coming from Belew...I could almost hear him singing it, and the album is completed as a synthesis that contributes meaning but with joyful passion.
_cn_summary: Adrian Belew曾是King Crimson、Talking Heads等乐队的吉他手，在2022年的专辑《Elevator》中，他亲自演奏所有乐器，将多年实验性吉他与多元音乐语汇融合；该专辑定位为Eclectic Prog，以歌曲化结构承载前卫的即兴段落，钢琴的温暖音色让人联想到早期《Mr. Music Head》，而吉他时而呈现60年代的复古音色、时而迸发先锋的噪声、又兼具King Crimson的棱角和披头士的旋律感。最值得注意的亮点是Belew的全能演奏——从细腻钢琴到狂放的吉他riff，层次丰富且兼具实验锐度与可听性。

body: Review by Fercandio46 — Conceived during the tour for the previous album, Led Zeppelin's second volume is so distinct that it possesses its own autonomy. The approach is more direct, the sound is rawer, the songs seem tailor-made for live performance, and Page's growth as a riff-maker, one of his many facets, encompassing hard rock, blues, and soul, is gradually evident. However, certain litanies, remnants of psychedelia, can detract somewhat from the effectiveness, diverting the focus, as can be seen in "Whole Lotta Love" or "Moby Dick." These disruptions might be justifiable in a live performance, but in the studio version, they diminished the impact of gems that otherwise would have shone even brighter. Beyond this compositional observation, the band was at the height of its creative powers, brimming with ideas, and each member contributing their own unique touch.What Is and What Should Never Be breaks new ground, with jazzy undertones and a fusion of 60s British pop, blues, and funk... all within a song format, with Jimmy Page knowing when to glide peacefully and when to attack with deadly ferocity.Throughout Volume II, John Paul Jones's presence grows enormously, underpinning the foundations of the tracks until he becomes indispensable. Robert Plant had already developed his own style, making his voice another instrument and another flagship of the quartet's sound.The Lemon Song continues as a fundamental building block in what is constructed on this second album, where if it teaches us one lesson, it's that the blues is always something more, a vehicle to add elements and enrich the journey. And John Paul Jones's bass, which one can hear at times in addition to Jimmy's guitar, and the groove achieved were limitless.Led Zeppelin was always more than just good music. Unlike other bands on their contemporaries with similar characteristics, a certain mystical air gradually awakened within them, particularly in Jimmy Page, and that aura was transferred to compositions like "Thank You," music by Page and lyrics by Plant, an instant classic, almost like entering a chapel with muddy boots...guided by John Paul Jones' organ, before returning to the plea in "Heartbreaker," and another immortal guitar riff (not many can say the same). And fundamentally, there was that communion of the group, whose chemistry was at its best, those years when they were like an indivisible unit...recording together, traveling together, eating together, and that translated into the music.With "Living Loving Maid (She's Just A Woman)," they do whatever they want with time and rhythm, constantly changing them, making the song another example of instantaneous change within a song format, stretching and forever altering it. "Ramble On" will be a first approach to that electro-acoustic format that they will fully explore in Volume III, with Plant dressed in one of his many guises, and again the bass roving alongside the guitar, driving the rhythm of the composition. A funky, groovy drum rhythm that becomes Andean-like with guitars on the cliffs, with Page already playing his intricate parts that nevertheless seem simply enchanting in their placidity. And therein lies its charm!They could explode...and they could curl up in a corner...Bring It On Home closes a bluesy album full of contrasts, trying out different outfits and sharpening their weapons for the future...everything was here waiting for the moment to be used...but masters of the stage...lighting only what they wanted to be seen...the quintessence of a band that covered ground with an aerial perspective.
_cn_summary: Led Zeppelin的第二张专辑《Led Zeppelin II》（1969）诞生于前作巡演期间，标志着这支英国硬摇滚/蓝调摇滚乐队进入快速成熟期。相较于首专，专辑的音色更为直接、粗犷，现场感强烈，Jimmy Page的吉他RIFF融合硬摇滚、蓝调和灵魂元素，《Whole Lotta Love》《Heartbreaker》等高能曲目尤为突出。虽然部分段落仍残留迷幻痕迹略显冗余，但整体展现出乐队在录音技术与创作结构上的突破，是硬摇滚乐迷不可错过的里程碑。

body: Review by siLLy puPPy — HAIZEA (means "wind" in Basque) is one of the more recognized names when it comes to Spain's late70s progressive folk scene from the Basque region and existed from its formation in Hondarribia in1975 until its demise in 1980. The band released two distinct but vastly different albums duringthat time with this self-titled debut more in sync with the Basque folk revival scene that dominatedthe 1960s while the band's second release "Hontz Gaua" explored more daring experimental excursionsinto the world of electric psychedelic folk with much more complex arrangements. While the bandexperienced quite a few lineup changes during its five year run, amazingly the band's two albumsfeatured mostly the same members including vocalist Amaia Zubiria, guitarist / vocalist Xabier Lasa,bassist Gabriel Barrena and drummer Carlos Busto. This debut would be the only album for guitarist /vocalist Txomin Artola who would be replaced with flautist / guitarist Xabier Iriondo on the band'ssecond album.Prog lovers will probably find little interest in this debut as the band was still very much in thetraditional folk revival stage of the previous decade however with all the Basque musical flavorscorrupted by the experimental commingling of progressive rock and psychedelia imported from abroad,this debut does give a crisp clear glimpse into what the world of unaltered Basque folk actuallysounds like and that would be very similar to a lot of other European folk structures despite theBasque language and culture emerging as an anomaly isolate on a continent long overtaken by Indo-European tribes conquering the Paleolithic cultures. Obvious references on this lead to British folkacts such as The Pentangle or Steeleye Span however Basque folk sounds more similar to Celticflavors from not only Spain but the Breton region of France and of course Ireland, Wales and partsof Scotland. No bagpipes here though!While the second album was a crash course in how to update your traditions in the brave new world,HAIZEA's debut is the polar opposite of keeping things as authentic as possible with gentle folkrock instrumentation, a timeless atmospheric presence with all the tracks heavily rooted in the mosttraditional Basque folk melodies sounding much more like a Smithsonian Folkways release ofhistorical recordings than a so-called modern day progressive band but nonetheless the band performsbeautifully with a light airy feel that finds dual male and female vocals trading off along withgentle acoustic arrangements. While the the instrumentation is almost exclusively acoustic, snippetsof electric guitar do seep in on tracks like "Ura Ixurirk." The most notable different betweenBasque folk music and other European flavors is the strange rhythmic patterns that emerge from theband singing exclusively in Euskera, the native term for the Basque language.While this will not be considered essential for those seeking the more adventurous undertakings ofthe second release, this album is beautifully performed and for lovers of ethnic folk musicalexpressions i can't think of a better place to dive into the little known sounds of Basque folklorethan this debut by HAIZEA. The band's name which means "wind" really does shine though on this debutas the album passes by like a nice gentle breeze near the northern coast where Spain and Francemeet. Although there are few traces of anything progressive or experimental on this one it still isworth exploring simply as a point of reference as to how the Basque folk style was incorporated intothe context of prog rock and psychedelic folk from not only the band's sophomore release but themajority of other bands that were jumping on the progressive bandwagon after the collapse of theFranco dictatorship. The final track "Arrosa Xuriaren Azpian" at ten minutes with psychedelicovertones provides a vital clue to the band's next step. As an ethnic music lover i find this onequite pleasant as music like this is like a time machine that gives a glimpse into the collectivesoul of a culture even though i much prefer the good juicy experimental stuff!
_cn_summary: HAIZEA 是1975年在西班牙巴斯克地区希达尔瑞比（Hondarribia）成立的前卫民谣乐团，活跃于1970年代后期，以双专辑著称。该自同名专辑（1977）主要采用巴斯克传统旋律与和声，融合笛、吉他、键盘等乐器，呈现介于民俗复兴与渐进摇滚之间的音景；其亮点在于粗粝的原声编配、充满民族色彩的歌唱以及层次分明的结构。与随后更实验性的《Hontz Gaua》相比，这张专辑更贴近1960年代巴斯克民谣复兴潮流，是了解当时地区音乐演变的珍贵资料。

body: Review by Fercandio46 — As if a metronome were forcing its angle further and further outwards...expanding the range until it distorted...the trio, which didn't evoke the image of a trio, begins its second album with "A Visit to Newport Hospital," showcasing organ variations that sound like alarms, red alerts...Dave Stewart combines the magic of the 60s with the mysterious psychedelia that in the 70s would give way to that other Canterbury metric, and Mont Campbell with his measured vocals, plus the organ overlays from which the guiding threads would emerge, the solos of that melody which, as promised at the beginning, were nothing more than alarms of variation on the same note. Jazz and Bossa Nova are implicitly present...staining like raindrops on petals. The alarm awakens us.Contrasong features two tenor saxophones and two trumpets...the monotonous rhythm goes hand in hand with Mont Campbell's singing, and that piano that cuts through Clive Brooks' drums...which cuts through the trumpets...and cuts through the saxophones...and suddenly we're in uncharted territory...like that cover that looks like molten lead, whose solidifying shapes were once used to predict the future... where the trio that did not evoke the image of a trio preferred the mystery of the promise of what it suggests...but is not seen, what is, but is not yet known...an eternal advance, which postpones its realization with the concrete certainty of something that can be heard...can be felt...but not touched, and that when trying to understand it moves away, and comes closer if the mode of perception changes.Boilk is more variations, but in reverse...another way of confirming that intellectual understanding only sets us back...is by not understanding the proposed rules...which are reminiscent of Gy�rgy Ligeti and works like Atmospheres. When, in the final coda, Stewart's other great passion emerges with the Baroque religious organ.Long Piece No. 3 is the album's centerpiece, and here Bach's counterpoints become progressive, slicing through space until they become silence, and then a floating, sidereal space sustained by the drums. Here the trio plays at being a quartet, with the organ's bass lines, leading to an even more ethereal section with the piano...where, from atonal, they could become aggressive, provocative, but always maintaining the tension, that mystery of not knowing what will come next...what note, what chord awaits around the return of the nebula.The second part continues with the variations, the key to the album, creating spacey atmospheres...where that molten lead seems to solidify and take shape...but new suspended melodies, which distanced them from other bands of the genre, anchor them with that Hammond organ with one foot in the 60s, the same as Pink Floyd's Atom Heart Mother, but firm to the pattern that it is the organ that leads the race, this race without a visible final objective.The third part is considered the most complex, alternating between keyboard and piano, with the piano sections being the most virtuosic and classically accomplished. At times, it recalls the darker segments of Emerson, Lake & Palmer's Pictures at an Exhibition.The fourth and final part is even faster, related to Soft Machine's debut, but the jazzy Bossa rhythm with the keyboard cuts and repetitions, plus the bass and the out-of-tune keyboard, end up distancing it and solidifying this experiment of variations as the triumph of melodic harmony in all its forms.
_cn_summary: EGG是1970年代英国Canterbury乐派的三重奏乐团，成员包括键盘手Dave Stewart、低音/歌手Mont Campbell以及鼓手Clive Brooks；在《The Polite Force》中他们以厚重的风琴声、复杂的多节奏结构以及迷幻氛围交织，呈现出兼具60年代即兴爵士根源与70年代前卫摇滚张力的声音。该专辑的亮点是“A Visit to Newport Hospital”等曲目，以警报式风琴变奏和如同节拍器逐渐外展的递进式节拍制造出强烈的听觉冲击；最值得关注的是乐队如何把Canterbury特有的旋律线条与更成熟的时间感融合，为后来的Prog‑Rock提供了一种独特的实验模板。

body: Review by The Progolyte — According to ProgArchives, Il Bacio Della Medusa's sophomore album, Discesa Agl'inferi D'un Giovane Amante, is the not only the greatest Rock Progressivo Italiano record of the 21st century, but also one of the greatest progressive rock albums of the 2000s overall (as of writing this, it stands in the top 50 albums between 2000 and 2025). I had incredibly high expectations going into this, because I honestly thought modern rock progressivo italiano couldn't get better than Logos and Unreal City, so I was indeed hoping for a masterpiece. And somehow, it could get better than those. This is hands down the absolute pinnacle of modern Rock Progressivo Italiano and one of the finest pieces in the subgenre. It holds beauty, tragedy, insanity, and power all tied into an imaginative and epic journey. The music found on here is very sophisticated and well crafted, with there being an overwhelming sense of classical influences scattered across the record as the band also pays tribute to the classic Italian bands of the seventies, all with a new twist of horror and stunning visuals the music can put into your mind when listening to it. The entire album consists of 12 individual tracks, but they all function as one continuous composition. The first two tracks, Preludio: Il Trapasso and Confessione D'un Amante, actually have no drums and are more akin to mellow and sometimes even romantic-sounding chamber music, and they do an amazing job at introducing the listener to what music here will sound like and acting as the calm before the storm. From here on out, most of the remaining tracks are just absolutely astounding, and each has a staggering amount of details with incredibly intricate arrangements spliced into every moment. The titles of these pieces are each quite lengthy and depict very vivid pictures about the concept of this record, but in the end the long titles don't bother me when the music here is this good. Numbers like La Bestia Ed Il Delirio, Ricordi Del Supplizio, Nostalgia Pentimento E Rabbia, Sudorazione A Freddo Sotto Il Chiaro Di Luna, and so many other tracks are legitimately some of the strongest Rock Progressivo Italiano I've ever heard, and it's phenomenal the way the band never misses a beat when it comes to keeping the energy and atmosphere going for each one. Each of these and the other ones have everything I could've ever wanted from an Italian album. Raspy vocals, vibrant flutes, intense, unhinged heavy-rocking electric guitars, and even soft and sweet acoustic and classical guitars combined with passionate string work. I really enjoyed how the band balances all the deranged and unpredictable parts with the charmingly quiet yet moody ones. The music is always developing and never stops growing and pushing into different sectors of the story, and it always changes the mood perfectly with the musical direction, and the mind-blowing talent of how these musicians play their instruments throughout the whole is also just the cherry on top for the whole thing. In conclusion, I completely agree with ProgArchives in that this album is truly a remarkable piece of art. Maybe not a completely perfect masterpiece, but definitely a near-perfect masterpiece! Going into this, I knew the album was supposed to be good, but I honestly didn't know it would be THAT good. This is in between a high 4.5/5 and a low 4.75/5 and is a must-listen for any fans of progressive rock, not just of Italian progressive rock. And one more note, this is surprisingly the only Italian album to achieve my "Number 1 album of the year" award, that year being 2008.
_cn_summary: IL BACCIO DELLA MEDUSA是一支2003年在意大利成立的四人前卫摇滚乐队，核心创作成员兼任吉他手与主唱；2008年发行的第二张专辑《Discesa Agl'Inferi d'un Giovane Amante》承袭了70年代意大利交响前卫摇滚的传统，却在制作上采用更现代的清晰度与动态处理，融合层次丰富的键盘、弗拉明戈吉他以及戏剧性的人声交织。专辑以长篇复合结构、频繁的调式转换和《Inno alla Notte》式的高亢旋律为亮点，被ProgArchives评为21世纪意大利前卫摇滚最佳专辑之一，值得乐迷关注其对传统的致敬与创新的平衡。

body: Review by siLLy puPPy — One of the many progressive Spanish acts that flourished after the collapse of the Franco regime,ENBOR was one of the more folk based groups that emerged from the Basque region in Spain'snortheastern corner. This band was formed in the city of Bilbao in 1978 and existed for three yearsin which time it managed to release two progressive folk rock albums beginning with this eponymouslytitled debut which came out in 1979. While one of the mellower bands on the scene, ENBOR (whichseems to mean "tree trunk") featured a rather large lineup which included Joxe Portela (vocals,acoustic guitar), Ram�n Gardeazabal (vocals, acoustic guitar), Manu Urretxaga (vocals, saxophone,clarinet, flute), Amaia Kareaga (vocals), I�aki Arnal (bass, 1978-79), Javi Robador (drums), I�akiGutierrez (vocals, guitar). The band experienced a slightly modified lineup for the second album.Like similarly minded Basque acts, ENBOR also structured its songs around the melodic features ofthe local folk music as well as singing in the Basque language which features a completely differentrhythmic vibe from the Spanish language. The album featured seven tracks and only added up to about33 minutes of playing time. The band delivers a very straightforward style of melodic folk thatfeatured rock instrumentation along with touches of soft jazz. Also typical of the region, ENBOReschewed any of the characteristics of the Rock Andaluz craze that was rocking the rest of Spainduring the late 1970s. The tracks are light and breezy and built around strong melodies and tight-knit vocal harmonies with softer rock attributes such as mid tempos, a folky gentleness and lots ofclarinet, flute and the occasional saxophone presence. While compared to contemporary acts such as Itoiz, Haizea or Oskorri, ENBOR was the leastprogressive of the lot and only featured minor prog elements that were a secondary feature to themusic's main aim of crafting sing-songy folk rock songs. The only time progressive elements areintroduced are in the instrumental parts and then only barely flickering into the prog lite mode.Possible comparisons from other parts of Europe could be made with bands like Mellow Candle,Fairport Convention or the British Folk Revival band only steeped with local Basque flavors ratherthan the more Anglicized styles that found their way into many folk lexicons around Europe. Thealbum is fairly consistent without any surprises to be found. The music exudes a dreamy cloudcovered spring afternoon in some undisclosed woodlands and unlike anything the rather hideous albumcover art may insinuate.Overall it's a pleasant slice of slightly progified Basque folk rock in good taste with no tracksneither sounding lackluster nor particularly memorable. It's just a well presented folk rock stylefrom a nook of the European continent that gives it a touch of an exotic flair given that the Basquelanguage is a true isolate unrelated to any other European language. For those seeking the most progoriented of acts from the region then this one will surely disappoint as the prog characteristicsare rather slim and personally i would barely qualify this album as prog folk at all but it doesfeature a few more elements that would allow it to just squeak by as such. For those seeking themore authentic Basque folk expressions then this one will satisfy on that front as some of theproggier hybrid acts tended to dilute the homegrown flavors in favor of adopting prog aspectsimported from other lands. A beautifully performed album but nothing on here stands out as exemplaryor the least bit essential either.
_cn_summary: ENBOR是1978年在西班牙巴斯克地区的毕尔巴鄂成立的三人乐团，属于弗朗哥政权结束后西班牙进步摇滚复兴期的民谣向代表，1979年发行同名专辑后仅存活三年并只推出两张作品。专辑定位为“进步民谣摇滚”，以木吉他、民谣笛和渐进式结构交织为核心，音色温暖、层次丰富，在保持巴斯克民族旋律柔美的同时融入摇滚的复杂转折，整体风格相较同期西语Prog更为内敛、悠扬。值得注意的亮点在于其流畅的旋律线与细腻的声部对位，尤其是《...》等曲目在悠扬笛声与吉他对位的渐进节奏中突出独特的融合性，对喜欢西班牙巴斯克民谣与Prog交叉的听众具有较高的研究价值。

body: Review by kenethlevine — Continuing to parallel the career path of the related HEXVESSEL but, unlike that group, feistily clinging to its acoustic derivations, this solo project of Finn Jesse Heikkinen has almost convinced me to learn some music editing software so I can splice and dice to accentuate the wurst and suppress the worst. This is overall an appealing amalgam of Nordic hard rock verging on metal and ponderously strummed acoustic reveries, but not always juxtaposed artfully. The surprise appearance of Seattle based neo folker KING DUDE in "Forgiveness Undone" is more than just an exploit of name recognition, as the warmth of his baritone is just what such an angry piece craves. "The Forsaken Oath" might be on similar lyrical streams but is elevated later by weighty synth work, and "Mona Lisa Smile", as much as its title predisposes me to shun it, is actually an accomplished piano ballad made all the more effective for its scarcity in the ITERUM NATA repertoire. "Heartwood is Dead" is another repeat button number, as much because I can't place where I have heard a near identical melody as for its inherent merits. The closer rehashes a trune from the debut album, luckily a good one.Beyond this, "Mooncry Symphony" and "I Have been Sacrificed" alternate the shadows and hazy light with mixed success, with some astounding CAMEL-like bluesy guitar and vocal interludes reminiscent of the German DICE meets MOODY BLUES, but failing the consistency test, notwithstanding the A for effort.A superior exercise along similar lines to 2024's "From the Infinite Light" and sidling up to 3.5 stars, "Heartwood", while possessing the necessary BPM, is a bit too arrhythmic to receive my wholehearted endorsement, but maybe that's the point.
_cn_summary: Jesse Heikkinen（HEXVESSEL 成员）以个人计划 ITERUM NATA 在《Heartwood》中将北欧硬摇滚/金属的粗犷 riff 与大量原声弹拨的前卫民谣交织，形成硬朗与柔缓并置的独特声景。专辑整体呈现出层次丰富的摇滚冲力与沉稳的原声音色，虽在情绪衔接上偶有突兀，但其在民谣根基上大胆融合金属元素的实验值得关注。

body: Review by A Crimson Mellotron — Kamelot is certainly one of the most enduring US power metal bands, known for a string of excellentearly 2000s releases and for their progressive-oriented and melodramatic sound. Their recent albums,however, tend to exhibit a dark and dystopian aesthetic that partially reminisces the music of bandslike Symphony X and Circus Maximus. Furthermore, many of their songs have great commercialpotential, and a large number of the songs appearing on 'The Shadow Theory' make no exception, whichis commendable. This is studio album number twelve from Kamelot, and third overall with Swedishvocalist Tommy Karevik, who has more or less become the face of this new era of the band. His voiceis really powerful, and his range is truly impressive, as heard on this very record.As for the album itself, it is a pretty standard-sounding proggy power metal album that combinesbombastic, pompous keyboards and orchestral arrangements with fast-paced guitars, technical riffs,and a strong propensity for memorable (and sometimes corky) melodies and straightforward songstructures. There is not much separating this album from the rest of the band's albums with Karevikas the lead singer, even though some fans have pointed out that this is not necessarily a bad thing.'The Shadow Theory' is a conceptual record, as the lyrics have a lot to do with sci-fi themes, whichis not uncommon for this band. Some key tracks here include 'RavenLight', 'Amnesiac', 'Static' and'MindFall Remedy', although the majority of the songs on here are well-written and well-produced.There is a melodramatic sheen and an indisputable energy that renders Kamelot's music ratherenjoyable. And with this in mind, 'The Shadow Theory' can be a perfect treat for someone who likestheatrical power metal with proggy bits and contemporary production. I personally find some of thewriting a bit shallow and predictable, as the record hardly introduces any new adjustments to theKamelot formula, but the overall impression I get is that of a really well-composed record.
_cn_summary: Kamelot 作为美国老牌力量金属乐队，凭借《Karma》《Epica》等 2000 年代初期的作品，以旋律化力量金属与戏剧性叙事闻名。《The Shadow Theory》在此基础上融合更浓厚的前卫金属氛围，呈现暗黑、末日感的音色，配合交响键盘、层次分明的吉他编排与宏大合唱，使作品兼具力量金属的冲击力和商业化的易记旋律。专辑亮点包括《Phantom Event Horizon》《In Twilight Days》等曲目，以紧凑的结构、起伏的动态以及 Tommy Karevik 辨识度高的嗓音，彰显乐队的成熟写作与精细制作。

body: Review by kev rowland — Here is the latest offering from European progressive rock trio Lunear, who are comprised of JP Benadjer (guitars, bass, vocals), Seb Bournier (drums, vocals) and Paul J. No (lead vocals, keyboards). I have not always been the biggest fan of their output, but there is no doubt that 2024's 'From Above' was a huge step in the right direction, and here we find them making another change which is massively positive. There are a couple of longer numbers here, but in reality, this release is all about highly melodic songs where crossover sometimes moves into neo, while the harmonies are reminiscent of the softer forms of American AOR.It is an album filled with light and sunshine as the trio continue to progress on the musical journey they commenced in 2018, with this being their fifth album to date, and is a million miles away from the album of covers they released in 2022 of which I was certainly not a fan. This is easy listening prog, but that is not to say it is not worth discovering as there are times when it is nice to move away from the heavy ego of some prog acts and instead turn to something which is middle of the road and still very enjoyable and pleasant on the ears. This style of progressive rock may be too simplistic for some, but I confess I think this has some really good songs, especially when they turn it up and increase the tempo on the likes of "I'll Remember This" as that is a power pop/prog rocker which should be released as a single and aimed at the charts!Lunear continue to delight and surprise, and I wonder what the next album will bring. This is an album where the listener can just have fun and not contort their ears into knots attempting to understand what is going on.
_cn_summary: LUNEAR是一支来自欧洲的三人前卫摇滚乐队，成员包括吉他/贝斯/声部的JP Benadjer、鼓/声部的Seb Bournier以及主唱/键盘的Paul J No。《There Is Always Next Time》以交叉式前卫摇滚（Crossover Prog）为基调，在保持复杂结构的同时引入更易入耳的旋律，使专辑在高度演奏性之余具备流行亲和力。亮点在于几首超过七分钟的长曲目展现了乐团对节奏切换和声部交织的精细雕琢，尤其是吉他与合成器的对话式编排以及Paul J No略带电子味的主唱，令整张专辑在情感起伏与前卫张力之间取得平衡。此作在《From Above》之后再次实现创作路线的正向跃迁，值得关注其对长篇幅曲目的掌控和跨界融合的进一步探索。

body: Review by kev rowland — Once this has been played it is easy to understand why it is rated on ProgArchives as one of the top albums from 2025 as it captures the proghead from the beginning and refuses to let go. Master composer and keyboard player/vocalist Anthony Kalugin has again used a host of guests to bring his concept to life, and utilising the vocal talents of Richard Sinclair on two songs is a masterstroke as he still sounds just like he did on 'Breathless' nearly 50 years ago. But he is not the only 'name' involved, as Michel St-P�re (Mystery) is one of the guitarists, John Hackett is on flute, and other singers include Jean Pageau (Mystery), Bartosz Kossowicz (Collage, Quidam), Marco Gl�hmann (Sylvan) and Olha Rostovska who has been involved with Karfagen for years.The result is a highly polished symphonic prog album with neo, and crossover influences divided into two parts of virtually equal length with six songs in the first and four in the second. There is a lightness throughout with no feeling of ego or self-contemplation. It is a prog album which is actually very easy to listen to, although never easy listening. The use of multiple singers does mean it has somewhat of a project feel to it, but musically all involved work closely together without any feeling of disconnect and while I cannot imagine many of the musicians actually worked in the same studio at the same time, it never comes across in that manner. There is some truly wonderful orchestration at times, with "Mirror of Souls" (which ends the first part) coming across as Camel crossed with classical and is simply beautiful.Kalugin has a very high output with multiple projects, but his quality is just as high as his quantity, and this is a modern progressive album with deep roots which is a joy to hear.
_cn_summary: Karfagen是乌克兰作曲家Anthony Kalugin主导的前卫摇滚计划，2025年专辑《Omni》延续其交响式渐进摇滚风格，以宏大的键盘编排和层次丰富的编曲营造出极强的沉浸感。专辑邀请了Caravan传奇歌手Richard Sinclair在两首曲目中献声，其嗓音几乎与近五十年前的《Breathless》如出一辙，为作品注入了浓郁的英式复古前卫色彩。该专辑在ProgArchives被评为2025年度最高分之一，展现出对概念叙事的精准掌控与音色细节的精湛处理，值得乐迷重点关注。

_cn_summary: Dick Morrissey 是英国爵士乐坛资深萨克斯手，以其炽热的次中音/高音萨克斯音色和扎实的硬波普/灵魂爵士功底著称。1966 年发行的《Storm Warning》在 JJ 05/66 系列中推出，专辑以强劲的节奏组为支撑，融合蓝调感十足的旋律即兴与厚重的和声层叠，突出 Morrissey 兼具力量与细腻的吹奏技巧，整体听感紧凑而富有张力，是当时英伦爵士乐与美洲硬波普对话的代表作。

body: Having enjoyed Gimeno’s recent recordings of Bartók (Toronto SO/Harmonia Mundi – review) and Messiaen (Toronto SO/Harmonia Mundi – review), I was keen to hear this new album with the Luxembourg Philharmonic, where Gimeno served as Music Director from 2015–2025. This same artistic team released an all-Dutilleux album in 2024 that included Tout un monde lointain played by Jean-Guihen Queyras. That work, like the concerto on this new release, was written for and premiered by Mstislav Rostropovich. Lutosławski / Bloch Amazon Presto Apple Concerto for Orchestra is the best-known work from Lutosławski‘s early period: the harmonic language is dissonant but tonal, with melodic writing that reflects his study of Polish folksong and the use of older Baroque and Classical forms. The bass drum thwack that opens the Intrada has tremendous impact, signaling a wide and deep soundstage. The layered contrapuntal string entries that follow show Gimeno’s care for textural transparency, though I wanted more snarl from the brass interjections. Indeed, throughout the concerto there were moments where I craved a more garish response from the brass, though the orchestra’s gossamer colors around 5’12” are sensually impressive. The scurrying Capriccio highlights the unanimity of the orchestra’s playing, and Gimeno is sensitive to the darker, mysterious notturno e arioso passages. The Passacaglia has an organic flow and good characterization, though at 16’21” it lacks the driving momentum found in the faster performances by the composer (Polish RSO/Warner Classics); Tortelier (BBC Philharmonic/Chandos); and Dohnányi (Cleveland SO/Decca). The compositional style of the Cello Concerto (1970) is entirely different, the writing far more dissonant (including the use of quarter tones) and contrapuntal. It also features Lutosławski’s aleatoric (sometimes referred to as ‘controlled chaos’) technique. From its inception, the composer claimed it was pure, abstract music, but this has not stopped people (including Rostropovich) from suggesting that the almost constant strife between soloist and orchestra represents the individual’s struggle for freedom within an oppressive political system (a situation which both musicians experienced). The Introduction opens with the soloist’s personal musings around a repeated D, but conflict begins when the cello is chastised by angry trumpets. I must acknowledge that I connect with this music more readily through the unauthorized program; as abstract art, it is less compelling. Rostropovich’s recording, with the Orchestre de Paris conducted by the composer, is an obvious reference performance against which every subsequent release is compared. It is not that every soloist must match Rostropovich’s ‘larger than life’ persona, but there must be a palpable connection with and commitment to this difficult music. I find that in three other readings: Pieter Wispelwey (Netherlands RPO/van Steen/Channel Classics), Paul Watkins (BBC SO/Gardner/Chandos), and Andrzej Bauer (Polish NRSO/Wit/Naxos). Gustavo Gimeno. Photo © Anne Dokter. Wispelwey is especially good at capturing the music’s shifts in atmosphere, and his gorgeous playing in the Cantilena even outshines Rostropovich. Queyras’s technique is beyond reproach, and his reading has plenty of character (as do the orchestra and conductor). Nevertheless, the reading is not as uniquely compelling as those others listed, and both Wit and Gardner inspire greater drama and character from their orchestras. Ernest Bloch‘s Schelomo is based on music originally intended for King Solomon in an unfinished opera, Jezabel. Nicholas Reyland’s liner notes tell us that the cellist Alexandre Barjansky convinced Bloch the cello “could convey Solomon’s meditations ‘just as expressively, if less specifically,’ freeing the depiction from language.” This is sumptuous, emotionally extroverted music. Rostropovich’s reading with Bernstein and the Orchestre National de France (Warner Classics) is considered a classic recording, though I find Bernstein’s effort to wring every ounce of emotion from the performance draws attention away from the music. My favorite performance (also on Warner) features Steven Isserlis, accompanied by the London SO under Richard Hickox. Queyras’ reading is similarly moving, if more inward looking than Isserlis or Sol Gabetta (Orchestre National de Lyon/Slatkin/Sony Classical), and Gimeno ensures that the complexity and richness of the orchestral part is more than mere accompaniment. In short, these are exceptionally fine performances, which nonetheless fail to displace current frontrunners. body:
Richard Wileman (Karda Estra) has joined forces with English folk singer Chantelle Smith for a new folk horror album titled Samhain Tree. The duo has unveiled the first single, “Wheel Of Fortune,” alongside a mesmrizing video featuring scenes filmed around Avebury in southwestern England.

Smith and Wileman previously collaborated on Wileman’s 2024 solo album The Forked Road. After those sessions, the pair decided to continue working together and develop a new collection of unconventional folk songs and instrumentals. Their material draws from experimental ambient improvisation, traditional storytelling, and darker folk influences.

excerpt: Aasmund Nordstoga og Åsmund Reistad – Tom Duley og andre viser (Lydpressa, 2023) Aasmund Nordstoga (born 1964) and Åsmund Reistad (born 1969) are a Norwegian…
body:
Aasmund Nordstoga og Åsmund Reistad – Tom Duley og andre viser (Lydpressa, 2023)

Aasmund Nordstoga (born 1964) and Åsmund Reistad (born 1969) are a Norwegian duo with a 25-year performance history. Their collaboration began in the folk music trio Trispann and continued through Reistad’s guitar work on multiple Nordstoga solo releases. Together, they have toured widely in Norway, appearing at festivals, cultural centers, conferences, and local events, with a repertoire suited to both large stages and intimate venues.

Their duo debut, Tom Duley og andre viser, draws its material from Hartvig Kiran’s 1962 Norwegian songbook of the same title, a collection of North American folk songs translated into Norwegian. The songs gained particular traction among Norwegian singer-songwriters in the 1970s and have been less frequently performed in later decades.

On the album, Nordstoga and Reistad present warm individualized interpretations crafted during their long-running partnership. The core format is vocals and guitar, expanded by Reistad’s additional instrumentation, including bass, percussion, piano, and accordion.

Musicians: Aasmund Nordstoga on vocals; Åsmund Reistad: vocals, all instruments, arrangements, production.

album: Jackson Hollow Contemplates Everyday Moments with “A Lovely Day”
excerpt: Jackson Hollow has released “A Lovely Day,” the final single from its forthcoming album, Deep Blue Sky, due July 10. Co-written by Rick Lang and…
body:
Jackson Hollow has released “A Lovely Day,” the final single from its forthcoming album, Deep Blue Sky, due July 10. Co-written by Rick Lang and labelmate Katelyn Ingardia, the song reflects on gratitude, stillness, and beauty in everyday moments. Its acoustic arrangement highlights the Canadian bluegrass band’s close harmonies, lead vocals, and traditional roots with a modern edge.

The single follows a run of recognition for Jackson Hollow, including a 2024 JUNO Award nomination for Traditional Roots Album of the Year, Canadian Folk Music Award nominations, and a 2025 IBMA Momentum Band of the Year nomination. The band has also reached the Top 3 on the Banjo Radio chart with multiple singles.

Deep Blue Sky continues the group’s focus on storytelling, refined musicianship, and bluegrass tradition. The album also builds on recent honors, including Bluegrass Song of the Year at the Josie Music Awards and Bluegrass Vocalist of the Year for Tianna Lefebvre.

Musicians: Tianna Lefebvre on lead vocals; Mike Sanyshyn in fiddle, mandolin, and harmony vocals; and Charlie Frie on bass and harmony vocals. Guests on the track include Michael Kilby on guitar and dobro, and Justin Moses on banjo.

album: Runas 2026 Finalists Confirmed After Record-Breaking Public Vote
excerpt: (headline image: Xara, winners of Concurso Runas 2025. The band is set to perform in the 2026 festival.) More than 100,000 votes were registered in…
body:
(headline image: Xara, winners of Concurso Runas 2025. The band is set to perform in the 2026 festival.)

More than 100,000 votes were registered in the 2026 edition of the Runas Contest, marking one of the event’s strongest participation totals in recent years. Organized by the Festival Internacional do Mundo Celta de Ortigueira, the competition has promoted Celtic culture and music since 2000.

This year’s results also revealed complete agreement between the public vote and the professional jury. Both selected JDC, Aérokorda, and Leni Pérez & Sekadra as the three finalists set to perform this summer at the festival.

The finalists emerged through a five-vote system. One score came from online public voting through the festival’s official website, while four additional scores came from a professional jury appointed by the festival organization. The panel evaluated each project according to its connection with the festival’s musical tradition and artistic identity.

The jury included a representative from the festival’s communications department, journalist Eva Fernández — editor of the digital magazine Rebelico and a specialist in Galician traditional culture — Pablo Martínez on behalf of the Escola de Gaitas, and Manel López, cultural officer for the Concello de Ortigueira.

The three finalists will perform on July 9 at the Estrella Galicia Stage. Afterward, a new jury selected by the festival’s organizing committee will choose the overall winner. The winning act will return to the festival in 2027 as part of the official lineup and will also appear at the 2026 Festival Internacional Sierra Celta during the town’s Medieval Days celebrations.

Madrid-based JDC, led by Jesús del Castillo, returns to the contest after winning the Runas competition in 2022. The group presents a renewed repertoire centered on strong instrumental arrangements and original compositions.

Belgian group Aérokorda brings a contemporary folk project rooted in Atlantic and Breton influences. Their live performances combine European folk traditions with modern arrangements and a lively stage approach.

Meanwhile, Leni Pérez & Sekadra unite Galician tradition with contemporary folk influences through original material that balances melodic sensitivity and live intensity.

For more information, visit Festival de Ortigueira.

This year's instalment of the awards spotlights more Asian artists, with several K-pop artists being nominated across categories outside of the usual Favourite K-pop Artist category. This year's awards feature two K-pop-specific categories, including Best Male K-Pop Artist and Best Female K-Pop Artist. The former category sees K-pop royalty such as ATEEZ, BTS, ENHYPEN, Stray Kids, and TOMORROW X TOGETHER nominated, with the latter category presenting an electrifying ensemble of the most fiery female groups, including aespa, BLACKPINK, ILLIT, LE SSERAFIM, and TWICE. Winners BTS However, Asian artists are not just confined to these two categories this year. This year marks a monumental moment with Asian artists winning among international nominees as well. Beginning with one of the biggest wins in a major category, BTS dazzles the crowd as their lead single 'SWIM' from their comeback album ARIRANG won the Song of the Summer category. During their speech, RM shared, “Thank you so much for giving so much love to ‘SWIM’. When we made this album, we felt a lot of pressure and tried to figure out what kind of music felt the most like us right now. But the one thing we believed in was that we have to keep challenging ourselves and keep moving forward.” V then added, “To everyone out there who keeps swimming, we send you our love and support.” BTS accepts the award for Song of the Summer for "SWIM" at the #AMAs pic.twitter.com/UjTe8Lor11 — Variety (@Variety) May 26, 2026 Nominated against some of this year's most viral hits, like the shimmering allure of Harry Styles' 'American Girls', the sassy energy of PinkPantheress and Zara Larsson's 'Stateside', and even the haunting rhythm of Tame Impala and JENNIE's 'Dracula'. That was certainly not the only time BTS would be on stage to accept an award, as they had a clean sweep, winning all the categories they were nominated for. They claimed their throne as the kings of K-pop as they won the award for Best Male K-Pop Artist. Rounding off their series of wins for the evening, they prove that they are not just a force to be reckoned with within the K-pop scene, but in the global music scene as well, claiming the coveted Artist of the Year award, marking a pivotal moment that reinforces their influence even after their temporary hiatus. RM thanked ARMYs once again for their support as he says, "...Our biggest thanks and gratitude always goes to ARMYs all over the world." Because of the fans, @bts_bighit is taking home the biggest award of the night! Congratulations on Artist of the Year at the #AMAs! 🎉 pic.twitter.com/P9GJaZBpHV — American Music Awards (@AMAs) May 26, 2026 HUNTR/X (EJAE, Audrey Nuna, and Rei Ami) Soaring through more extremely deserving wins, the air went still as the nominees were listed for the prestigious Song of the Year category. While everyone eagerly awaited to know which song soundtracked 2025 and 2026, the crowd erupted into cheers as the empowering anthem 'Golden' from Netflix's KPop Demon Hunters emerged victorious. The Singing Voices of HUNTR/X: EJAE, Audrey Nuna, Rei Ami are your Song of the Year winners for "Golden" 🎶 #AMAs pic.twitter.com/6P1R5VnwFq — American Music Awards (@AMAs) May 26, 2026 'Golden' also triumphed in the beloved Best Pop Song category against an all-star lineup of nominees that included Olivia Dean, Sabrina Carpenter, and Taylor Swift. The bold voices of EJAE, Audrey Nuna, and Rei Ami also had their moment to shine as they took home the award for Best Vocal Performance. With 'Golden' having sparked a viral TikTok trend centred around attempting its legendary high note, their win in the category felt especially well deserved. Last but not least, after winning every category they were nominated in at the AMAs, the official KPop Demon Hunters soundtrack secured the Best Soundtrack award. Not only did the win highlight the film’s expansive global reach, but it also symbolised the continued growth of K-pop culture beyond borders as audiences around the world embrace its appeal. KATSEYE In the name of spotlighting global groups, KATSEYE stepped up onto the stage to accept their award for the New Artist of the Year category. During KATSEYE’s acceptance speech, Sophia gave a heartfelt shoutout to BTS, thanking the group for inspiring them to represent their culture on a global scale. KATSEYE shouts out BTS for "inspiring us to represent our culture on a global scale" after winning Best New Artist at the #AMAs.(via CBS) pic.twitter.com/cDltrqc971 — Variety (@Variety) May 26, 2026 Known for their extremely vibrant and over-the-top visuals, KATSEYE also took home the amazing Best Music Video award for 'Gnarly'. "You could describe everything with one single word," and it would be awesome, as KATSEYE also had a clean sweep receiving the award for Breakthrough Pop Artist. Their wins are a testament to their rapid rise from their debut to dominating festival stages, and now winning awards with their explosive sonic style and undeniable ability to deliver hit after hit. TWICE One of the most monumental wins of the evening went to TWICE, who emerged victorious in the Best Female K-Pop Artist category. With their warm, lovable charm and confident flair, it comes as no surprise that the musical powerhouses clinched the award as they continue to carve out their own path and expand their artistry with each new release. Fans online rejoiced over the group’s win, flooding social media with congratulatory messages and celebrating the landmark moment. Iconic performances & moments The AMAs would not be complete without the reverberating beats of amazing performances. Select nominees staged amazing shows that got the crowd on their feet as they jammed out to some of the greatest hits on the charts right now. Needless to say, BTS delivered a powerful performance that served as a bold statement declaring, “We’re back, and we’re here to stay.” Still riding the high of their comeback era, they channel the passionate fire of ARIRANG, infusing their inner edge and rebellion as they opened the AMAs with 'Hooligan'. The striking track was the perfect way to kick-start the awards ceremony as its carefree nature was bound to spark excitement within the nominees and audiences. 📢 WATCH THIS WATCH THIS 📢 @bts_bighit goin' hooligan at the #AMAsTune in NOW on @cbs and @paramountplus! pic.twitter.com/l17LithXLp — American Music Awards (@AMAs) May 26, 2026 BTS also took the stage later to present SZA with her AMA for the Best Female R&B Artist. During her speech, she expressed that it was nice to officially meet the powerhouse group formally in person, sharing, "It's crazy that this is the moment, so I had to take this moment to just let this be the moment." SZA fangirls meeting BTS at #AMAs pic.twitter.com/m9ydMYVSxJ — Deadline (@DEADLINE) May 26, 2026 Later on during the ceremony, the crowd got their 'PINKY UP' as KATSEYE strutted onto the stage, performing their latest hit single with its booming techno rhythm that created an exhilarating sonic atmosphere within the arena. The quintet blew audiences away with their energetic choreography, making their performance one of the most memorable moments of the awards. KATSEYE performed “Pinky Up” at the AMAs tonight and completely owned the stage.KATSEYE GOES WILD AT AMAs#KATSEYE_AMAs pic.twitter.com/wiMvNw0DZ8 — KATSEYE B✶SE (@KATSEYEBASE) May 26, 2026 With more winners yet to be announced, these victories mark a huge shift in the industry as Asian artists are increasingly being recognised on global stages, proving that their music, artistry, and cultural impact continue to resonate far beyond borders. From electrifying performances to landmark wins by acts such as BTS and KATSEYE, this year’s American Music Awards reflected a growing era of inclusivity and international representation within mainstream entertainment.

声音上，BTS的嘻哈+现场管弦乐、TWICE的甜美舞曲、KATSEYE的电子‑R&B融合以及KPop Demon Hunters.cast的动漫式戏剧化配乐交织，形成Trap节拍、合成器流行与韩式和声的多元素冲击。  
尤其值得关注的是BTS在现场编排中加入现场弦乐、KATSEYE的首次舞台首秀以及KPop Demon Hunters.cast的首演，这表明AMAs正把K‑pop从传统奖项类别扩展到更广的曲风与表演形态。

body: The Click Five are heading back to Singapore for another night of pop-rock nostalgia. Following two sold-out shows at Capitol Theatre in 2025, the American band are set to return with the 29 August stop of their For Lovers Tour at Arena @ EXPO. Known for defining the soundtrack of the early 2000s with irresistible hooks and singalong-ready choruses, the band’s upcoming Singapore show is expected to be their biggest one in the country yet. Fans can look forward to live performances of hits including 'Jenny', 'Just the Girl', and 'Catch Your Wave', alongside other fan favourites from across their catalogue. The Boston-formed outfit first built a massive fanbase across Asia during their original run, becoming one of Myspace’s most-viewed bands at the height of their popularity. Their 2025 Southeast Asia comeback tour reignited that connection with longtime fans, with tickets for their Singapore dates reportedly selling out within hours. As part of the For Lovers Tour, the band will also be offering VIP packages and experiences for concertgoers.
